title: Ultra-processed food exposure and adverse health outcomes: umbrella review of epidemiological meta-analyses
authors: Lane MM, Gamage E, Du S, Ashtree DN, McGuinness AJ, Gauci S, et al.
population: 45 pooled analyses from 14 meta-analyses of cohort, case-control and cross-sectional studies, 9,888,373 participants in total
authorConflicts: Eight authors are affiliated with the Food & Mood Centre, Deakin University, which has received research funding from Be Fit Food, Bega Dairy and Drinks and the a2 Milk Company and philanthropic funding from several foundations; FN Jacka is an unpaid scientific advisory board member of Zoe Nutrition; other declared interests are listed in the article.
result: Direct associations for 32 of 45 pooled analyses (71%). Convincing (class I): cardiovascular disease mortality RR 1.50 (95% CI 1.37 to 1.63; GRADE very low), type 2 diabetes RR 1.12 per 10% increment (1.11 to 1.13; moderate), prevalent anxiety OR 1.48 (1.37 to 1.59; low) and common mental disorders OR 1.53 (1.43 to 1.63; low). Highly suggestive (class II): all-cause mortality RR 1.21 (1.15 to 1.27; low), obesity OR 1.55 (1.36 to 1.77; low). Cancer mortality HR 1.00 (0.81 to 1.24). GRADE: 4 moderate, 22 low, 19 very low. No included meta-analysis was funded by a producer of ultra-processed food; none reported the funding sources of its primary studies (AMSTAR 2 item 10).
